claims.text: Calling toString on an Output<T> in Pulumi produces placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` instead of the resolved value.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ titled 'Output value errors' describing symptoms of treating a Pulumi output as if it were a plain value.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Pulumi Cloud returns the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" when an update conflicts.
On Apple Silicon Macs, x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs in Pulumi.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds providing bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.
Converting a Pulumi Output to a string directly instead of via apply does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message.
In TypeScript, the resulting string contains text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use apply or pulumi.interpolate.
In TypeScript, calling JSON.stringify() on an Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, converting an Output to string yields text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported` and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Python, passing an Output to json.dumps() fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; Output.json_dumps() should be used instead.
In Go, passing a pulumi.StringOutput where a string is expected is a compile error.
In C#, the resulting string contains text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use Apply or Output.Format.
Setting environment variable PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true (TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an Output to string throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text.
String-composition helpers: pulumi.interpolate and pulumi.concat in TypeScript; Output.concat/Output.format/Output.json_dumps in Python; pulumi.Sprintf/pulumi.JSONMarshal in Go; Output.Format in C#.
The apply callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished, so an outer variable assigned in it is undefined when read earlier.
Most resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values; a resource's logical name cannot be an output.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on an Output is generally always true because the Output object is evaluated; in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error.
Values known at program start, such as stack config read with pulumi.Config, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Passing an Output as a resource logical name or loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, range(some_output) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the output object itself.
A later, separate stack can consume the first stack's outputs through a StackReference.
Pulumi has no supported way to synchronously block and extract a resolved value from an Output.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. res.Outputs in Go).
Pages exist at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/ and /all/ and /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences and /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
